checks: A proper section gives at least one coefficient of each sign. If these were the only two nonzero coefficients, the asymmetric two-sided exponential density would have left derivative 1/[r(a+r)] and right derivative −1/[a(a+r)] at zero, violating C¹. Hence one orientation has at least two positive phases and one negative. Zero phases cannot change the density in this check.

In that orientation the centroid identity and accepted size bias apply for every index. Convolving f_V with the distribution of c_jE′, including negative c_j and the point mass when c_j=0, gives d b_j=∫₀∞ exp(−s) f_V(−c_js)/f_V(0) ds.

The tangent inequality for log f_V is valid at −c_js for either sign. If ℓc_j≥0 the ratio is at most one on the integration range, so b_j>1/d implies ℓc_j<0. When ℓ=0 the set of indices above 1/d is empty. For c_j=0 the ratio is identically one. Reversing orientation leaves the centroid fixed, flips the sign of every nonzero margin together, and preserves positivity, C¹ regularity and log-concavity of the reflected density.

For a strictly positive capacity row with a proper minimum, normalize by its positive threshold. The Schur theorem gives the two-positive phase count, properness gives a negative phase, and the accepted density fact supplies the hypotheses. The same section and margin signs persist under the positive scaling to the original threshold.
